salient_findings: Hypoechogenic subcardial mass on the posterior gastric wall
Recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site after resection
key_facts: 48-year-old woman
7-year history of submucosal tumour
Tumour located below the esophagogastric junction
Presented with melena and progressive anemia
Hemoglobin level was 7.5 g/dL
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed a 70 × 50 × 55 mm hypoechogenic mass
Lesion was resected endoscopically by a piecemeal technique under general anesthesia
Histopathology reportedly confirmed a lipoma
Recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site six weeks after resection

differentials: Intra-abdominal desmoplastic small round cell tumor
per_call: Intra-abdominal desmoplastic small round cell tumor

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent bleeding submucosal gastric tumour with high risk of malignancy

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial histopathology confirmed a lipoma, but recurrence suggests possible malignant transformation

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal tumour with bleeding and recurrence, raising suspicion for a smooth muscle tumour

shortlist.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site, with a large size and hypoechogenic appearance on CT

shortlist.label: Carcinoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal tumour with bleeding and recurrence, with a possible neuroendocrine origin

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a submucosal tumour and recurrent bleeding, along with the tumour's location and size, is consistent with a gastrointestinal stromal tumor, especially given the initial histopathology report of a lipoma may be questionable due to the aggressive behavior of the tumour.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are rare in the gastrointestinal tract and the patient's tumour location and behavior do not strongly support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: While leiomyosarcomas can occur in the gastrointestinal tract, the patient's presentation and tumour characteristics are more consistent with a gastrointestinal stromal tumor

rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's tumour is described as a submucosal mass, which is less typical for gastric adenocarcinoma, and the histopathology report does not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Carcinoid tumor
rejected.why: Carcinoid tumors are typically smaller and have a more indolent course than the patient's tumour, which has shown aggressive behavior with recurrent bleeding
